title: Targeted Asymmetric-Layer Perturbation with Slower Annealing
scientific_hypothesis: The four most asymmetric layers (11, 15, 19, 20) in the 24-layer dichroic stack dominate the shallow gradient region behavior; applying ±12% targeted perturbation bounds to these layers while maintaining broader bounds elsewhere, combined with slower annealing decay (0.98), will enable the optimizer to escape local minima and improve dual-band spectral separation.
design_principle: Localized thickness freedom at transition-critical layers preserves the established high-performing stack structure while allowing fine-tuning where spectral band edges are most sensitive. Slower annealing maintains optimization momentum through shallow gradient regions identified in iteration_16.
proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Total finite layers: 24.
design_variables: Layers 11, 15, 19, 20: bounds centered at iteration_16 best candidate values with ±12% range
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain robustness score above iteration_16 baseline
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer constraint)
Thickness bounds ensure manufacturable values 50-280 nm
Alternating HfO2/SiO2 sequence compatible with standard deposition processes
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Gradient-based optimization with annealing for non-convex thickness spaces
Theory that transition-region layers control band-edge spectral features
expected_advantages: Focused perturbation reduces search space dimensionality while targeting critical layers
Slower annealing prevents premature convergence in shallow gradient regions
Builds directly on iteration_16 best candidate (target_score 0.909)
known_risks: ±12% bounds may be too restrictive if optimal solution lies outside this range
Slower annealing increases computation time per optimization run
Local optimization may still converge to nearby local minimum
execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Initialize layer thicknesses from iteration_16 best candidate: [73.74, 173.68, 63.72, 117.85, 89.90, 91.13, 236.11, 73.97, 133.26, 90.19, 61.73, 87.94, 212.45, 89.67, 61.74, 83.26, 62.17, 89.15, 163.46, 214.22, 56.62, 87.41, 180.24, 56.30] nm. Apply thickness bounds: layers 11, 15, 19, 20 (0-indexed) have bounds centered at their initialization values with ±12% range; all other layers have bounds 50-280 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with annealing decay factor 0.98. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence, unpolarized. Score objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band, maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Return best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, thicknesses_nm, and run_status. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
revision_reason: Refinement of route_02 per feedback directives: implementing targeted ±12% perturbation on layers 11, 15, 19, 20 and switching annealing decay from 0.95 to 0.98 to address shallow gradient convergence observed in iteration_16.
